newsitem.title: USA: Midwest dealers take 5c protection corn, 20c soy.
newsitem.headline: Midwest dealers take 5c protection corn, 20c soy.

text.p: In anticipation of sharp losses in CBOT futures, U.S. Midwest grain dealers were taking widespread protection of up to five cents per bushel on corn and 20 cents per bushel on soybeans.
"We're taking five cents on corn and 20 cents on beans, and that is everything, not just old crop," one Ohio dealer said.
CBOT corn and soybean futures were expected to open sharply lower in response to higher-than-expected acreage figures from the U.S. Department of Agriculture.

The USDA put 1997 soybean acreage at 68.80 million acres. That figure compared to a trade average of 65.85 million. The government put corn acreage at 81.416 million acres, which was higher than the trade average of 80.92 million.
